verses.1: A certain woman from the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “My husband, your servant, has died, and you know that he was a man who revered the LORD. The creditor has come to take my two sons as slaves.”
verses.2: Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house.” She said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.”
verses.3: He said, “Go out and get empty jars from all your neighbors, as many as you can get. Don’t be stingy.”
verses.4: “Then you will go in and shut the door behind you and behind your children, and pour oil into all those jars. When one is full, set it aside.”
verses.5: So she went out from him and shut the door behind her and behind her children, while they were bringing the jars to her, and she was pouring.
verses.6: When the jars were filled, she said to her son, “Bring me another jar.” He said to her, “There are no more jars.” The oil had stopped.
verses.7: So she came and told the man of God, and he said, “Go and sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your children will live on what is left.”
verses.8: One day Elisha passed through Sunem. A prominent woman was there and recognized that he was a holy man of God passing through constantly.
verses.9: She said to her husband, “Look, I have realized this man is a holy man of God. He passes through our land consistently.
verses.10: Let’s build him a small room on the wall and set for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp. He can rest there whenever he comes to us.”
verses.11: So it happened on one day when Elisha came there, he rested in the room.
verses.12: He said to his servant Gehazi, “Call this woman from Sunem.” He called her, and she stood before him.
verses.13: He said to her, “Tell me, have you done all these generous gestures for us? Is there something I can do for you? Is there a word you want me to say to the king or to the commander of the army?” She said, “I live among my own people.”
verses.14: He asked, “What should I do for her?” Gehazi his servant said, “She has no child, and her husband is old.”
verses.15: So he called her, and she stood at the door.
verses.16: He said to her, “At this time next year you will hold a son.” She said, “No, my lord, do not deceive your servant.”
verses.17: But she became pregnant and gave birth to a son at the appointed time, the time that Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.18: When the child grew up, one day he went out to his father to the harvesters.
verses.19: He said to his father, “My head, my head!” His father told the young man, “Carry him to his mother.”
verses.20: He carried him and brought him to his mother, and he lay on her lap until midday, then he died.
verses.21: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
verses.22: She called to her husband and said, “Please send one of the boys and one of the donkeys. I will run to the man of God and return.”
verses.23: Her husband said, “Why are you going to him today? It’s not a new moon or a Sabbath.” She said, “Peace.”
verses.24: She hitched the donkey and said to her servant girl, “Go on, ride. Don’t hold me back from riding unless I tell you.”
verses.25: So she went and arrived at the man of God on Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her coming from a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, it’s the woman from Sunem.”
verses.26: “Now run to meet her and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’ She will answer, ‘Peace.’”
verses.27: She arrived at the man of God on the mountain and clung to his feet. Gehazi tried to push her away, but the man of God said, “Let her be, for her soul is in anguish. The LORD has hidden this from me and not told me.”
verses.28: She said, “Did I not ask you for a son? Didn’t I tell you not to deceive me?”
verses.29: Elisha said to Gehazi, “Tie up your belt and take my staff in your hand. Go ahead, but if you meet someone, don’t greet them, and if someone greets you, don’t respond. Place my staff on the boy’s face.”
verses.30: The mother of the child said, “By the life of the LORD and by your soul, I will not leave you.” So he got up and followed her.
verses.31: Gehazi went on ahead and placed the staff on the boy’s face, but there was no sound and no response. He returned to meet Elisha and reported, “The boy has not awakened.”
verses.32: Elisha went into the house and saw the boy lying dead on his bed.
verses.33: He went in and shut the door behind them both, then prayed to the LORD.
verses.34: He climbed onto the boy and lay across him, placing his mouth on the boy’s mouth, his eyes on the boy’s eyes, and his hands on the boy’s hands. He pressed hard, and the boy’s flesh warmed.
verses.35: He went away and walked around the house once, then came back and pressed hard on the boy seven times. The boy opened his eyes.
verses.36: Elisha called to Gehazi, “Call this woman from Sunem.” He called her, and she came to him. He said, “Pick up your son.”
verses.37: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. She took her son and went out.
verses.38: Elisha returned to Gilgal when a famine had struck the land. The sons of the prophets were sitting before him, and he said to his servant, “Boil a large pot and prepare a meal for the sons of the prophets.”
verses.39: One of them went out to gather herbs in the field. He found a wild vine and gathered a bunch of wild gourds, filled his cloak, and brought them back. He cut them up and added them to the pot, not realizing what they were.
verses.40: When the men began to eat from the meal, they cried out and said, “Death is in this pot, man of God!” They could not eat it.
verses.41: Elisha said, “Bring me some flour.” He threw it into the pot and said to Gehazi, “Serve this to the people so they may eat.” There was no more harmful thing in the pot.
verses.42: A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread made with new grain and a jar of honey. He said, “Feed these to the people so they may eat.”
verses.43: His servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they may eat. For the LORD said, ‘They will eat and there will be leftovers.’”
verses.44: He set it before them, and they ate and had leftovers, just as the LORD had said.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "a small room on the wall" – the Hebrew is literally "a little chamber," which may be a small annex or alcove added to the house.
- v. 31: "placed the staff on the boy’s face" – the staff is likely symbolic of Elisha’s authority and role as a prophet.
- v. 34: "pressed hard" – the Hebrew term indicates a vigorous, possibly violent action, possibly signifying a supernatural intervention.
- v. 41: "Bring me some flour" – the Hebrew uses "kemach," which is usually "flour," but in context it may refer to a specific type of grain or powder.
